question.text: How do we start a category the world doesn't have a name for yet, and become the one that leads it?

history.text: How might we lead with security without becoming another cyber company?
history.reason: Reframed from a defensive question (how not to look like cyber) to category creation, at a level of ambition that matches the founders.

answer.headline: Every token is born in a data center. 12 Planes makes the data center as intelligent as what it creates.
answer.body: The most important machines on earth are still run the way they were 30 years ago: in pieces, by hand, behind fences. 12 Planes sees every plane at once, from the ground to the token, and makes all of it better every day. It starts with security, because trust comes first. It doesn't stop there.

history.text: Nobody owns calm, provable trust in the place where AI runs. 12 Planes can.
history.body: Security brands borrow their authority and sell fear. Data center brands sell parts. The brands that moved their category earned authority with one simple idea. The open space is authority 12 Planes earns itself, across the whole data center, starting with security.
history.reason: Elevated to match the new key question.

insights.headline: The problem has gone public
insights.body: In one week in November, Microsoft, the FAA and Chase failed within days of each other, drawing 6.4 million outage reports. None was a cyberattack. Each traced back to ageing equipment or a defect nobody had caught. Demand for compute keeps running ahead of what anyone can build, understand or secure.

history.body: AI infrastructure is moving faster than anyone can understand or secure it. Recent outages showed infrastructure nobody fully understands.
history.reason: Sourced and sharpened.

insights.headline: Accountability is the new test
insights.body: Around seven in ten Americans oppose an AI data center near them, and in November voters passed more than 20 measures to ban or restrict them. Data centers have become the visible face of the AI backlash. Transparency and proof count more than celebrity.

history.body: Data centers have become the visible face of the AI backlash. Transparency and proof count more than celebrity.
history.reason: Sourced and sharpened.

insights.headline: The race for the standard has started
insights.body: Irregular sets security standards for frontier models. Lava leads an OWASP top 10 for neocloud and AI data center risks. Standards are forming around single slices. Nobody yet speaks for the data center as a whole.

history.text: The race for the standard has started
history.body: Irregular sets it for models, Lava for neocloud risk. The data center as a whole is still unclaimed.
history.reason: Sourced and sharpened.

history.text: The race for the standard has started
history.body: Irregular sets security standards for frontier models. Lava now leads an OWASP top 10 for neocloud and AI data center risks. Standards are forming around the data center, but nobody yet speaks for the whole of it.
history.reason: Softened: Lava and OWASP already cover AI data center risks, so the data center is not unclaimed.

insights.headline: Security borrows its authority
insights.body: Analyst badges and leadership claims reassure buyers, but every brand sounds alike. Fear has moved from the copy into the names, and the words 'leader' and 'AI factory' are taken.

insights.headline: The data center has no story
insights.body: Everyone sells a part of the data center. Nobody speaks for the whole. The closest neighbours sell equipment and connection, not trust. Equinix is the exception with a clear one-sentence position.

insights.headline: Category leaders keep it simple
insights.body: One idea, one sentence, one image. The mission, not the feature list. Their authority is their own.

insights.headline: Security is the first plane, not the last
insights.body: Lead with security for 18 to 24 months, then operations, then autonomy. The bigger vision is shared step by step.

insights.headline: Calm, not fear
insights.body: The founders want trust and uptime as the value. Security should stop being the brake on the business.

insights.headline: A standard, not another vendor
insights.body: 12 Planes should write the standard for a sector that does not exist yet. A stamp of approval, like the FDA, and nothing that feels like cyber.

principles.headline: Earn it in public
principles.body: Authority in a new category can't be borrowed from analyst badges. It is earned in the open: what 12 Planes finds, what it fixes, and every extra nine of uptime.

history.body: Earn authority by showing what 12 Planes knows, instead of borrowing it from analysts and logo walls.
history.reason: Elevated copy.

principles.headline: Answer for the whole
principles.body: Everyone else sells a part of the data center. 12 Planes understands all twelve planes, from the dirt to the token, and stands behind every one.

history.text: Speak for the whole data center
history.body: Equinix owns connection. 12 Planes can own understanding and trust across every plane, from dirt to token.
history.reason: Elevated copy.

principles.headline: Confidence, not fear
principles.body: Fear sells locks. Confidence lets people build. 12 Planes is what lets AI go further, faster.

history.body: Uptime and trust are the value. Security is what lets AI go further, faster, not the brake.
history.reason: Elevated copy.

principles.headline: Make the complex feel simple
principles.body: The most complex system on earth deserves the simplest idea. One sentence, one image, and room to grow into.

history.text: The more complex the product, the simpler the claim
history.body: One idea, one sentence, one image. Short enough to remember, large enough to grow into.
history.reason: Elevated copy.

principles.headline: Start with security. Never stop there.
principles.body: Secure it first, then run it, then let it run itself. The brand moves as fast as the product, and never stands still.
principles.note: Marked in the deck as inspiration for Sprint 2 and activation, not a plan.

history.text: From stealth to standard, one layer at a time
history.body: Come out of stealth with one clear claim, prove it by publishing openly, then set the standard others measure against. The brand grows with the product from security to operations to autonomy.
history.reason: Elevated copy.

territories.name: The Architect
territories.archetype: The enabler as the one who designs the future, rethinking from first principles how intelligence should be built.
territories.idea: Twelve planes, from the dirt to the tokens. Looks like a flat stack, is really a three-dimensional problem. 12 Planes is the single view that holds every facet at once.
territories.role: 12 Planes designs how intelligence should be built, from first principles.

answers.how: Turns twelve planes, from the dirt to the token, into one designed structure that can be seen and turned.
Structure signals integrity, but says little about proof or the public.
The architect draws the blueprint others build to. A standard is a design.
Calm and precise, but cool. Confidence comes from order, not warmth.
The name is the idea. 12 Planes needs no explaining once you see the form.
New planes can be added, but a finished design can feel fixed.
First principles is the opposite of patching a 30-year-old stack.

territories.strongest: The most direct answer to starting and leading a category. It owns the name, the whole and the standard in one idea.
territories.risk: Can turn cold and abstract, closer to an engineering firm than a movement. Needs warmth and proof added.

territories.name: The Catalyst
territories.archetype: The enabler as the small, precise trigger for big change, where one trusted layer sets off a transformation across the AI economy.
territories.idea: A data center behaves like a living organism. 12 Planes is its immune system: it understands every part and notices the moment something is off.
territories.role: 12 Planes is the one trusted layer that keeps the whole system alive, and makes it better.
territories.line: Where the next leap in AI begins.

answers.how: An immune system understands every part of the body and how it acts. That is the whole data center, made legible.
Protective and trustworthy, but it works out of sight. It needs a way to show its proof.
It defines what a healthy whole looks like, a reference others can check against. It shapes the standard through the system rather than declaring it.
An immune system protects without fear. It is what lets the body go further.
Anyone grasps an immune system in a second. The most human metaphor of the three.
It learns, adapts and grows stronger. Security first, then operations, then autonomy, without changing shape.
Organic imagery feels alive, but less obviously like a leap in technology.

territories.strongest: The best answer to continuous improvement and to replacing fear with confidence. Explains the product better than any other territory.
territories.risk: Soft for a standard-setter, and close to biotech. The archetype (a trigger for big change) and the moodboard (an immune system) also tell two different stories.

territories.name: The Foundation
territories.archetype: The enabler as the ground a new industry is built on. Not the plumbing underneath, but the foundation that lets AI reach its full potential.
territories.idea: Every era of technology needed a foundation before it could take off. 12 Planes is laying the foundation for a new age of AI: an industry that does not exist yet, and a new relationship between people and AI built on trust. Built so intelligence can go further.
territories.role: 12 Planes establishes the industry a new age of AI will stand on.

answers.how: It speaks for the whole by being the ground the whole stands on. One foundation under every plane, so the data center reads as one thing, not a set of parts.

history.how: It speaks for the whole by speaking above the parts. Less about how the planes connect, more about what they make possible.
history.reason: Rated strong at the owner’s request.

answers.how: Foundations are trusted because they hold. Proof, like every extra nine, becomes evidence of an ambition, not a feature.
The one who lays the foundation sets the standard everyone builds on. The closest fit to Lior’s stamp of approval.
Confidence is the point of a foundation. It is what lets everything on top go further, faster.
One big idea anyone understands: before AI can reach its full potential, it needs a foundation.
The foundation stays, and what is built on it grows. Security, then operations, then autonomy are floors on the same ground.
Establishing an industry is the opposite of upgrading one. It speaks to the era, not the equipment.

territories.strongest: The biggest voice of the three. It speaks less to how 12 Planes works and more to why it exists: to establish an industry and change how we relate to AI, so it can reach its full potential.
territories.risk: Ambition without proof can sound like a slogan, so it needs the nines and the work to back it. The current moodboard still leans functional and retro, with a control-room look Dragos already uses. It has to move towards the scale of the ambition.

evidence.text: Landscape: two industries, data security and AI, meet in the data center. Around 35 players mapped across 11 segments.
Outages at Microsoft, the FAA, Chase and Apple drove 6.4 million U.S. Downdetector reports in a single week in November.
The FAA grounded every U.S. flight on 13 November after legacy equipment became unstable under a data flood. It found no sign of a cyberattack.
Congress's research service flagged the 4 h 45 min ground stop as a warning about how far critical systems lag modernisation.
Microsoft traced the 12 to 13 November Outlook outage to a latent defect introduced by a July update, compounded by failover traffic and reduced capacity.
Roughly seven in ten Americans oppose an AI data center in their area, 48% strongly, across every party group.
In November, voters passed more than 20 ballot measures banning or restricting data centers.
58% of U.S. voters say new data centers from big tech will mostly harm the country. A quarter support them.
On-demand GPU capacity is effectively sold out, TSMC capacity is sold out, and power has become a critical bottleneck.
AI chip production across logic, memory and packaging is the binding constraint on the compute build-out.
Demand is outstripping available capacity by nearly three to one in key Tier-1 regions (HyperFrame Research).
AI executives describe compute demand as almost unlimited. AWS says it will not have enough capacity to meet 2026 demand.
A gigawatt AI campus costs roughly $35 to $60 billion all in. Nvidia puts it near $60 billion, independent models nearer $38 billion.
Irregular raised $80M to set security standards for frontier models. Its SOLVE framework is used by Anthropic and the UK government.
Lava Security leads an OWASP Top 10 for neocloud and AI data center security risks, first published July 2026.
AI data centers are being built faster than they can be secured.
From the field: compute demand runs at two to three times available supply, and the pressure to bring capacity online pushes security down the list.

99% uptime allows about 3.65 days of downtime a year. 99.9% about 8.8 hours, 99.99% about 53 minutes, 99.999% about 5 minutes.
The Foundation territory explores .99, point99 and P99 as wordmarks, shown on a brushed-metal tile next to a 12 Planes website.
The product proposition, building compounding value: Protect, Perform, Progress.

present.title: 12 Planes · Sprint 1
present.note: Presentation copy may be shorter than the map. Every screen points to a node in the map, so "Why?" always opens the full rationale.

screens.eyebrow: Kontrapunkt for 12 Planes · Eclipse PortCo · 30 November 2026

screens.headline: Four numbers that frame the opportunity

items.label: Category
items.caption: AI compute demand against available capacity in key regions
items.more: AI is being built faster than anyone can build, understand or secure it. Capacity is sold out, and security is a minor line in budgets of tens of billions per site.

items.label: Competitor
items.caption: brands in our audit that speak for the data center as a whole
items.more: Security brands borrow their authority from analyst badges and sell fear. Data center brands sell a part: the hardware, the power, the connection. Nobody owns calm, provable trust across the whole.

items.label: Customer
items.caption: U.S. outage reports in one week of November
items.more: Microsoft, the FAA and Chase failed within days of each other. None was an attack. Each traced back to old infrastructure nobody fully understood. For operators, uptime is the business value of trust.

items.label: Culture
items.caption: Americans oppose an AI data center near them
items.more: Data centers have become the visible face of the AI backlash, and in November voters passed more than 20 measures to restrict them. Trust now has to be earned in public.

screens.headline: The leaders of new categories say one thing, simply.
From guarding the perimeter to securing the origin.
Five principles for leading a new category.
Three ways to lead the category.
screens.sub: All three are versions of The Enabler: 12 Planes does not build the AI, it makes it possible. Each territory tells that story differently, and answers what we found in its own way.

screens.headline: Seven jobs the brand has to do.
Which territory do we take into Sprint 2?
screens.sub: Reactions, not decisions. Then the brand narrative v1 in mid-December.

hidden.headline: Start with security. Never stop there.
steps: One clear claim, said by people who matter.

brandJobs.job: Make the whole data center legible
brandJobs.challenge: Infrastructure has outgrown anyone’s understanding, and every vendor sells one slice.
Security borrows its authority, and the public has turned against data centers.

brandJobs.job: Set the standard for the whole
brandJobs.challenge: Standards are forming slice by slice. Nobody owns the whole.
The category sells fear. The founders want uptime and trust as the value.
The more complex the product, the simpler the claim has to be.
Lead with security now, then operations, then autonomy, always improving.
AI cannot be built on infrastructure conceived 30 years ago. The brand must not look like an upgrade.

pov.headline: Lead with The Foundation. Build it with the other two.
pov.body: The Foundation gives 12 Planes the biggest voice: the company establishing an industry and changing how we relate to AI, so it can reach its full potential. It speaks to ambition, not function. The Architect gives it a system, rethinking how intelligence is built, and The Catalyst explains how the product works and keeps getting better.
parts: Where the next leap in AI begins
pov.note: Our point of view to react to, not a decision.

history.headline: Lead with The Architect. Borrow from the other two.
history.body: The Architect is the strongest answer to starting and leading a new category. It owns the name, the whole and the standard. It is also the coolest of the three, so it borrows: the immune system from The Catalyst to explain how the product works and how it keeps improving, and the nines from The Foundation as proof.
history.reason: Recalibrated to lead with The Foundation.

nameExploration.question: Can we bring the scale of the ambition into every part of the brand, including the name?
nameExploration.origin: The Foundation moodboard explored .99, point99 and P99 as wordmarks, drawn from Naor’s point that every extra nine changes what it means to be down.
nameExploration.ninesInsight: In a data center, 99% is failure. The value lives in the nines after the point. That is the strongest story .99 can tell, and also its biggest risk if read literally.

criteria.label: Easy to say, spell and find

options.name: Keep 12 Planes
options.for: Carries the whole, every plane from the dirt to the token. Already known to investors and design partners. Works as the system behind The Foundation.
options.against: Says nothing about trust or a standard on its own. “Planes” can read as aviation.

options.name: Rename to .99
options.for: Born from Naor’s own words. Short, iconic and typographic. Turns proof into the name.
options.against: Read literally, 99% is two nines, the downtime 12 Planes exists to end. Also reads as a price ending. Hard to say (dot or point?), search and register with leading punctuation. Names a metric, the most functional choice, just as The Foundation moves to ambition.

options.name: Rename to P99
options.against: A generic engineering term for 99th-percentile latency, and the name of an established conference for the same audience. Hard to own, and latency is not the 12 Planes story.

options.name: 12 Planes, with .99 as the mark of the standard
options.for: The company name carries the ambition, .99 carries the proof. Gives Lior’s stamp of approval a form: a data center can be .99 certified. Exactly the role the nines play in the recalibrated Foundation.
options.against: Two names to build. .99 still needs its story, the point every extra nine starts from.

nameExploration.pov: Keep 12 Planes and test .99 as the mark of the standard. If a full rename is on the table, now, before the stealth exit, is the cheapest moment to make it. But it should be decided against criteria, not because the wordmark looks good.
questions: What is the rename solving? Is 12 Planes failing a test, or is .99 simply compelling?
Should the name carry the ambition, or the proof?
How does a metric name age when the product moves to operations and autonomy?
What do investors and design partners already call the company?
Can we clear it? Trademark, domains and handles before any further design.

history.question: Should 12 Planes become .99?
history.reason: Reframed from a yes/no rename to the scale of the ambition across the brand.

proposition.headline: Building compounding value
proposition.sub: What 12 Planes brings. Each layer of value makes the next one possible.

items.name: Protect
items.body: Defend against threats from every direction. That covers physical, IT and OT attacks, and also the AI itself acting outside its bounds. The data stays where it belongs.
items.answers: Leads with security, as the founders want, and covers what single-slice vendors cannot.

items.name: Perform
items.body: Catch issues before they cause downtime. Credibility shows up as reliability, and that’s worth real money.
items.answers: Turns trust into uptime, the business value Naor describes, and proof the market can measure.

items.name: Progress
items.body: When people can trust AI with their data and their decisions, they use it for more. 12 Planes helps grow the whole AI economy, not just protect it.
items.answers: Answers the backlash with trust, and gives the ambition its reason: unlocking AI’s full potential.

lenses.name: Authority
lenses.insight: Security brands cluster where authority is borrowed and the product is the hero. The brands that moved their category sit opposite. Next to them, the space is open.

lenses.name: Role and promise
lenses.source: Kontrapunkt positioning axes. Placements are a draft.
lenses.insight: Standards are emerging, but through risk and urgency (Lava, OWASP). The calm, confident standard for the whole data center is still unclaimed.

competitors.name: Dragos
competitors.note: The only security brand with a mission larger than its product. The look still belongs to the control room.

competitors.name: Palo Alto Networks
competitors.note: The incumbent everyone is measured against. Scale is the message, little point of view.

competitors.name: CrowdStrike
competitors.note: The one-platform promise, told through threats. The opposite of calm proof.

competitors.name: Wiz
competitors.note: Proof a security brand can be warm. Too playful for the calm line the founders want.

competitors.name: Cerebras
competitors.note: Chips and systems. Sells compute, not trust.

competitors.name: Nebius
competitors.note: Neocloud customer as much as neighbour.

competitors.name: CoreWeave
competitors.note: Neocloud customer as much as neighbour.

competitors.name: Vertiv
competitors.note: Sells the hardware 12 Planes will watch over. As much partner as neighbour.

competitors.name: Schneider Electric
competitors.note: Products, not a point of view. Owns “AI factory” language with Nvidia.

competitors.name: Equinix
competitors.note: The closest neighbour with a real position. Owns connection. 12 Planes can own understanding and trust.

competitors.name: Cursor
competitors.note: Speaks to what people build, not the tool.

competitors.name: SpaceX
competitors.note: A mission large enough to grow into.

competitors.name: Palantir
competitors.note: Made software feel like infrastructure and named its category first.

competitors.name: Irregular
competitors.note: Sets security standards for frontier models. The model for owning a standard, with a reputational caveat.

competitors.name: Lava Security
competitors.note: Leads an OWASP top 10 for AI data center risks. The closest challenger for the standard, framed through risk.

toInvestigate.name: Uptime Institute and TIA-942
toInvestigate.why: They already certify data centers by tier. Any .99 standard mark would sit next to them.

toInvestigate.name: NVIDIA AI factory reference designs
toInvestigate.why: NVIDIA is defining what a good AI data center looks like, with Schneider and Vertiv as partners.

toInvestigate.name: Hyperscalers’ own tooling
toInvestigate.why: AWS, Microsoft and Google build this internally. Neoclouds first, hyperscalers later means they are future customers and competitors.

toInvestigate.name: OT security consolidation
toInvestigate.why: Claroty, Nozomi and Armis are moving up from industrial sites into data centers.

toInvestigate.name: Buyers, not brands
toInvestigate.why: Interview three to five neocloud operators on how they choose and who they trust. The audit so far is websites only.

enabler: All the territories are versions of one master archetype, The Enabler. 12 Planes does not build the AI. It makes it possible for AI to go further. Each territory tells that story differently.

drafts.was: Placeholder for 12 Planes product (initial solution for customers)
drafts.text: 12 Planes gives AI data centers a brain. One connected system that sees across power, cooling, hardware, networks, compute and security, so operators know what is happening, what is about to happen and what to do about it.

drafts.was: Copy from another client’s project (one engine tuned per industry, SAP and Oracle, manufacturing and logistics). Remove before anything is shared.
drafts.text: One operational model for the whole data center. Signals from cooling, power, hardware, networks and software come together in one model, so a change anywhere is traced across everything it touches. Trust builds step by step: first it watches and warns, then it recommends and a person approves, then it acts on its own within guardrails. Security, then operations, then autonomy.
Fewer incidents, caught before they cost. Faster answers when something does go wrong. Proof on demand, for customers, auditors and enterprise contracts.
Every plane in view. / The calm before every storm. / Know before it breaks. / Built so intelligence can go further.
